title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook — Incident Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status & Customer Comms
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s standard incident process, runbook format, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations, game day exercises, and templates for status page and customer communications. The goal is to ensure fast detection, consistent escalation, reliable mitigation, clear customer communications, and durable remediation actions with ownership and timelines.

Scope: Applies to all production services that serve customer inference requests (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private control plane) and platform dependencies (ingress, auth, billing, metrics).

Key contacts and ownership
- Incident Commander (IC): role assumed by on-call primary for the affected service. Responsible for leading the response, declaring severity, and coordinating communications.
- Primary responder: on-call engineer for the service. Executes runbook steps and performs mitigations.
- Secondary (backup): supports primary and takes over if primary is unavailable.
- On-call Manager: oversees rotations, escalations beyond team boundaries, and post-incident reviews.
- Customer Success / Support Liaison: drafts customer-facing messages and coordinates outbound comms for impacted accounts.

Severity definitions (use when declaring incident level)
1) SEV1 — System outage / customer-visible failure: major functional loss (e.g., API 5xx rate > 50% for 10+ minutes, inference throughput unavailable across region). Requires immediate paging and exec notification.
2) SEV2 — Degraded performance / partial outage: elevated errors or latency that meaningfully impact customers (e.g., 5xx rate 5–50% sustained or P95 latency > SLO + 200ms). Requires paging and team response within 15 minutes.
3) SEV3 — Minor incident / internal user impact: isolated errors, one account impacted, or non-customer-facing degradation. Address during business hours or next rotation.
4) SEV4 — Informational / planned maintenance: scheduled changes, rollout observations that do not require emergency response.

Alerting thresholds (examples)
- API 5xx rate > 5% over 5 minutes -> SEV2 page to primary.
- API 5xx rate > 50% over 2 minutes or complete regional outage -> SEV1 page to primary + manager + support.
- P95 latency > SLO + 200ms sustained for 10 minutes -> SEV2.
- KV cache evictions > baseline * 3 -> SEV2.

Incident lifecycle and runbook structure
All incidents follow a standard lifecycle: Detect -> Triage -> Mitigate -> Communicate -> Resolve -> Review. Each service must maintain at least one primary runbook that follows the template below.

Runbook template (plain text; include in service repo and Confluence)
- Runbook title: <service-name> — <symptom> (e.g., inference-gateway — 503 spike)
- Intent: short description of what this runbook covers.
- Pager criteria: specific alert names and thresholds.
- Immediate checks (first 5 minutes) — numbered list of commands and checks:
  1. Confirm alert source (Datadog / Prometheus alert).
  2. Check service health: kubectl get pods -n production -l app=inference-gateway; kubectl describe pod <pod> for restarts.
  3. Check upstream/downstream dependencies: redis/kv, model-store, auth.
  4. Tail logs: kubectl logs -n production <pod> -c inference-gateway --since=10m | grep ERROR.
  5. Check infra metrics: GPU utilization, host oom events, network errors.
- Hot fixes (actions to attempt during mitigation):
  - If pods failing readiness: kubectl rollout status deploy/inference-gateway; kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-gateway --to-revision=<n> if a bad deploy suspected.
  - If disk pressure / oom: cordon + drain affected node; scale up node pool; restart pods.
  - If model load failures: check model-store connectivity and recent model onboarding events; restart model-worker and monitor KV cache.
- Known safe workarounds: route traffic to fallback model variant (model-v1-small), reduce batch size, enable degraded mode (no-tool-calls) from feature flag.
- Escalation: when to page secondary -> on-call manager -> SRE lead -> VP Eng. Include Slack handle and phone numbers in the runbook header.
- Post-mitigation validation checklist: confirm error rate back to baseline for 15 minutes, confirm tail logs show resolved stack traces, run smoke tests against /health and a test inference call.
- Post-incident documentation: create incident ticket and fill postmortem template within 72 hours.

Example runbook excerpt: inference-gateway — 503 spike
Intent: Rapid mitigation for production 503 spikes affecting generation endpoints.
Pager: datadog.alerts.inference-gateway.5xx-rate > 10% over 5m -> SEV1.
Immediate checks:
1) Confirm alert -> Datadog -> confirm scope and affected region.
2) kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference-gateway
3) kubectl logs -n prod $(kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference-gateway -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -c inference-gateway --since=5m | tail -n 200
4) Check Redis / KV: redis-cli -h redis.prod cluster info; look for connection errors.
Hot fixes:
- If 503 caused by model-worker OOMs, set MODEL_WORKER_MAX_BATCH=8 and restart pods: kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-gateway -n prod; monitor for stability.
- If caused by a recent rollout, run kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-gateway -n prod and verify.

Escalation policy and contact matrix
- Primary -> 10 minutes of continuous paging attempts (Slack, phone).
- If no acknowledgment in 10 minutes, page Secondary (same team).
- If incident declared SEV1 and not mitigated within 20 minutes, on-call manager and SRE lead are paged.
- For cross-team impacts (networking, cloud provider, DB), SRE lead should coordinate cross-team war room and escalate to VP Eng if > 60 minutes unresolved with customer impact.

On-call rotations and schedules
- Rotation cadence: 1-week rotations as default for platform teams. Product/infra-heavy teams may choose 2-week rotations with manager approval.
- Roles per rotation: Primary, Secondary, On-call Manager (monthly), Pager Duty owner.
- Handoff procedure (start of rotation): outgoing engineer posts a short status note in #oncall-handoffs Slack channel with open issues, maintenance windows, and any ongoing investigations.
- Backup and time-off: primary must set an explicit secondary if unavailable for > 24 hours. Use the team calendar and PagerDuty overrides for coverage.

Game days (exercise plan)
Objective: validate runbooks, alerting, cross-team escalation, and customer comms under controlled conditions. Run 2–4 game days/year per team.
Sample game day scenario: regional API 5xx spike due to model-store throttling.
- Pre-game checklist: select participants (engineering, SRE, support, product), schedule 90-minute window, define success criteria, ensure no real customer impact.
- Execution: inject alert in staging or sandbox environment, observe detection, run runbook, escalate according to policy, prepare status page update mock, complete post-game retrospective.
- Post-game actions: update the runbook gaps, fix alert thresholds or dashboards, and track follow-ups in JIRA with owners and SLAs.

Postmortem requirements and template
All SEV1 and SEV2 incidents must have a written postmortem published within 72 hours; SEV1 requires a follow-up RCA meeting within 5 business days. Postmortem must include:
- Title, incident ticket ID, incident lead (IC), service(s) impacted, severity, start and end timestamps.
- Summary (1–2 paragraphs for execs).
- Timeline of events (bullet list with timestamps).
- Root cause analysis (clear statement of primary cause and contributing factors).
- Detection and mitigation: how incident was detected and the steps taken to mitigate.
- Customer impact: list affected customers, duration and measurable impact (errors, latency, failed requests).
- Action items (owner, due date, priority) — tracked in JIRA.
- Postmortem reviewer list and sign-off.

Postmortem example summary:
- Summary: On 2026-01-12 02:10 UTC, inference-gateway experienced a sustained 5xx rate increase peaking at 72% due to a model-worker memory regression introduced in a canary rollout. Primary mitigations included rollback of the deployment and scaling up worker replicas; service returned to baseline by 02:58 UTC. Root cause: a model-worker change increased memory usage under high load; contributing factors: insufficient pre-rollout load testing and missing OOM alerts on the worker.
- Action items: Add model-worker memory SLA tests (owner: S. Martinez, due 2026-02-15), add OOM alert (owner: M. Chen, due 2026-02-01), update runbook to include model-worker memory checks (owner: D. Kim, due 2026-01-25).

Status page and customer communications templates
All external communications must be coordinated with Customer Success and Legal for regulated customers. Use the following templates and trim for channel (status.redwood.ai, email, or in-product banner).
1) Initial public status page (short)
- Title: Partial outage affecting text generation API (region: us-west-2)
- Impact: Customers may experience increased 5xx errors or failed requests to the text generation endpoints. We are investigating.
- Updated: <timestamp>
- Next update: within 30 minutes or when new information is available.
2) Ongoing update (public)
- Status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating
- Details: Brief technical update (what we see, which services are affected, mitigation in progress).
- Customer impact: Which endpoints/accounts/regions affected.
- Next update: in 30 minutes / after next milestone.
3) Resolution message (public)
- Title: Incident resolved — text generation API restored (region: us-west-2)
- Summary: The issue was caused by <short cause>. We rolled back <change> and verified system health. No further action required by customers.
- Timeline: start — resolution timestamps.
- Follow-up: link to postmortem (published within 72 hours).

Customer support / enterprise email template (for impacted customers)
- Subject: Incident update: text generation API issues in us-west-2 (start: <timestamp>)
- Body (initial): Hello <Customer Name>, we are currently investigating increased errors affecting the text generation API in us-west-2. Our engineering team is actively addressing the issue. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. We apologize for the impact. — Redwood Inference Support
- Body (resolution): Hello <Customer Name>, the issue impacting the text generation API in us-west-2 has been resolved as of <timestamp>. Root cause: <short cause>. We rolled back the offending change and validated recovery. We will publish a detailed postmortem at <link>. If you experienced data loss or persistent failures please reply and we will prioritize follow-up.

Runbook hygiene and maintenance
- Owners: each service runbook must have a named owner and a biannual review date.
- Review process: owners must update runbooks after each SEV1/SEV2 incident and during scheduled reviews. Changes must be committed to the service repo and referenced from Confluence.
- Testing: automated smoke tests and synthetic traffic should run daily against critical endpoints; alarms should be exercised in game days.

Metrics and SLOs to track during and after incidents
- Error budget burn rate and remaining error budget (weekly).
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA): target < 5 minutes for SEV1.
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM): target < 30 minutes for SEV1.
- Mean time to recovery (MTTR): target < 60 minutes for SEV1; track for each incident.
- Post-incident action completion rate: % of actions completed by due date (target 95%).

Appendices
A) Pager escalation contact list (maintained separately): include PagerDuty escalation policies, phone numbers, and Slack handles.
B) Quick commands cheat sheet (copy into runbooks): kubectl commands, Datadog query examples, S3 model-store checks, GPU health checks.
C) Links: links to runbook repos, SLO dashboards, status.redwood.ai, PagerDuty policies, and support contact playbooks.

How to use this document
- Team leads: ensure this playbook is referenced in team onboarding and engineering onboarding.
- On-call engineers: keep runbooks current, practice with game days, and complete postmortems promptly.
- Product & Customer Success: subscribe to the status page and use the customer comms templates for impacted accounts.

End of document.
